model.architecture: Falcon-H1 is TII's fully-hybrid design: every one of the 32 layers runs a grouped-query attention branch and a Mamba2 selective-scan branch in parallel on the same input and sums them.

variants.quantization: int8 dynamic on linears + embedding (convs and the scan stay float); fp32 activations declared for GPU

recommended.reason: the Android path verified on a Galaxy S26 (S4 gate 2026-08-24): full delegation (55723 ops across 12 subgraphs) and a correct answer to the probe; 11.6 tok/s decode, engine init 18.1 s, peak 2128 MB. No same-device CPU control was taken, so this is the verified choice for the class, not a measured win over CPU

platform_notes: GPU execution is verified on macOS (Metal), iPhone 17 Pro (Metal), Pixel 8a (Arm Mali, OpenCL) and Qualcomm Adreno (Galaxy S26).
On low-end Android the GPU buys prefill and time-to-first-token, not decode (decode is memory-bandwidth-bound; CPU reads int8 weights, the fp32-activation GPU path reads expanded ones).
GPU runs with fp32 activations (declared in the bundle) — expect a corresponding memory multiple over CPU.
Multi-length prefill signatures (1–1024) are exported so the runtime picks tight chunks; the bundle carries the tokenizer and the stock ChatML-style Falcon-H1 chat template.
Usage example runs the GPU backend with `--backend gpu --cache no`.

Not a measured row: card reports iPhone 17 Pro gpu prefill_tps 111.5, decode_tps 14.0, ttft_s 1.49 (Performance — On device table (iPhone 17 Pro, cold start, single runs); runtime/run count not stated)
